who.label: Who it’s for
who.title: Your back has hurt for months. Maybe years.
who.body: You’ve heard it all and tried a lot. Mostly, you want your life back: gardening, carrying your kids, driving without thinking about it.
who.fact: About 9 times out of 10, back pain has no specific cause. You’re not a special case.
for: You’re an adult, and your back has hurt for months.
No serious cause explains it: this is non-specific low back pain.
You want to move forward at your own pace, without pressure.

water.label: How it works
water.title: Every effort waters your tree.
water.body: A small plan each day: a short read, a little movement, a moment for the mind and some walking. You do what you can.
water.end: Your tree grows with you, and it never wilts.

steps.label: Reading
steps.title: Your reading path
steps.body: 23 five-minute lessons, written by our doctor, also trained in physiotherapy, to understand your pain and regain confidence.

steps.label: Movement
steps.title: Your exercises
steps.body: 5 to 15 minutes, 2 to 3 times a week. Exercises chosen for you, shown in 3D.

steps.label: Meditation
steps.title: A moment for the mind
steps.body: 3 to 30 minutes of mindfulness, when the day or your back weighs on you.

steps.label: Walking
steps.title: Walk, at your pace
steps.body: As far as you like. Another activity elsewhere, like yoga or cycling, counts too.

pain.label: During your session
pain.title: The app adapts to your pain.
pain.body: After each set, you rate your pain. If it goes up, we ease off. If it’s going well, we move forward gently.
pain.easyBody: If your whole session goes like this: one more repetition next time.
pain.holdBody: You can keep going. Next time, same level.
pain.stopBody: Stop this exercise: it’s the right call. Next time, we start a little gentler. A 3-minute comfort moment is waiting for you.

screens.label: In the app
screens.title: One thing at a time.
screens.s1Body: A short program. Nothing to catch up on.
screens.s2Body: The lessons, one by one, across the landscape.
screens.s3Body: You choose how much time you have.
screens.s4Body: What’s getting easier, in your own words.

pros.label: Health professionals
pros.title: Support between your appointments, and after them.
pros.body: BackToHealth replaces neither your assessment nor your follow-up. It helps your patients with low back pain keep moving, understanding and caring for themselves, especially after their sessions.
pros.ctaTitle: Want to try it or share your feedback?
pros.ctaBody: We’re looking for clinicians to review the content and offer it to their patients.

cards.title: Screening first
cards.body: 8 red-flag questions. A positive answer points to a doctor or the ER.

cards.title: A clear pain rule
cards.body: Above 3/10: stop, lower level. Session at 2/10 or less: one more repetition, up to 12, then the next level.

cards.title: A biopsychosocial approach
cards.body: Exercise, education, mindfulness and walking, together, as practice guidelines recommend.

cards.title: What we don’t claim
cards.body: No diagnosis, no treatment, no published study yet. With people’s consent, we will measure what works.

team.label: Who we are
team.title: Three committed cofounders, in Montréal.
team.body: Medicine, software development and data science, brought together to help people live better with back pain.

people.name: Pierre-Henri Bao Heitz
people.title: Cofounder · Health expertise
people.bio: Physician, also trained in physiotherapy. He originated the clinical approach of BackToHealth, based on recent research on chronic low back pain, and validates all of its content.

people.name: Adrien Moevus
people.title: Cofounder · Application
people.bio: Medical student and developer. He is responsible for the design and development of the mobile app, and writes the guided meditations.

people.name: Antoine Moevus
people.title: Cofounder · Data, measurement and AI
people.bio: He is responsible for data, outcome measurement and artificial intelligence, and takes part in the development of the app.

items.q: Does it replace my doctor or physio?
items.a: No. The app complements your care. If something worries you, talk to a health professional.

items.q: What if it hurts too much, or I don’t feel like it?
items.a: Every activity has a “Not today” button. Flare-ups are part of the path: for 3 days, the plan eases off. Your tree and your progress are protected.

items.q: When does the app come out?
items.a: It’s in testing on iPhone and Android. Write to us to hear about the launch.
The price isn’t set yet. You’ll know clearly before launch.
French and English, following your phone. You can switch any time.
Protected, never sold. You can export or delete it any time. Research is optional and uses a code, never your name or email.

end.title: Your tree is waiting.
end.body: Write to us: we’ll let you know as soon as you can plant it.

footer.disclaimer: BackToHealth does not replace the advice of a health professional.

offer.label: The program
offer.title: Four programs to get you started.
offer.body: A few weeks to understand your back, move, meditate and walk. Then the app stays with you, for as long as you like.
offer.goalTitle: And after? We stay with you.
offer.goalBody: Your exercises keep adapting, you meditate your way, you keep your walking rhythm and you see how far you’ve come.

Mindfulness, then kindness toward yourself and what matters to you.

meta.title: The program in detail · BackToHealth / Crescendos
meta.description: Exercises and dosing, 23 lessons, meditation and walking: what’s in BackToHealth, for patients and health professionals.

program.label: The program in detail
program.title: What BackToHealth contains, step by step.
program.lead: For the curious and for health professionals: the assessment, exercises, lessons, meditation and walking, as they are in the app.
program.status: Clinical content being validated by our doctor, also trained in physiotherapy. It may still change.
g3: 10 to 30 min, or 3 min of comfort
g4: 8 weeks, then at your own pace
eval: 8 red-flag questions. A positive answer points to a doctor or the ER, and the program doesn’t start.
4 movement tests (flexion, extension, right and left rotation), with the pain felt. They set the starting exercises and their level.
1 to 3 activities to get back to, rated from 0 to 10 (Patient-Specific Functional Scale).
The rhythm: a little every day, light and active days, or a few chosen days.
program.familiesTitle: The exercises, from easiest to most demanding
program.medDaily: Between sessions: finding that state for a few moments, 30 seconds to 2 minutes, effortlessly.
follow: The chosen activities are re-rated about every 2 weeks.
The movement tests are repeated about every 4 weeks, to compare.
Pain is tracked over time, with a weekly summary.
During a flare-up, 3 lighter days: no exercise, comfort moments and gentle walking.
Data can be exported at any time.
program.philoTitle: A toolbox, not a takeover of care
program.philoBody: BackToHealth gives the tools and the first steps. The program stands on its own; going further elsewhere (Pilates, meditation, clinic follow-up) is even better. The person stays in charge of their path.
program.glanceNote: These are the lengths of the introductory programs. The app then continues, with no time limit.
after: Exercises keep adapting, with new challenges when a level becomes easy.
Meditation continues with the practice built, from 10 to 30 minutes.
Walking keeps its rhythm, or rises to about 2 hours a week.
Lessons stay available, and the movement tests can be redone.
Going further elsewhere (Pilates, yoga, meditation, clinic follow-up) is encouraged.
program.exIdea: Moving without fear, guided by pain. The movement tests set the starting exercises: extension, flexion, rotation, trunk stabilisation, then strength (upper body, squat, lunge, hips). Up to 3/10, pain is acceptable: it doesn’t mean damage.
program.exProgress: 3 sets of 10 to 12 repetitions. Session at 2/10 or less: one more repetition; at 12, the next level. Above 3/10: stop, and one level down. When a family’s last level becomes easy, a harder exercise from another family is offered.
program.exExample: Glute bridge: 3 × 10, then 3 × 11, then 3 × 12, then Bird-dog at 3 × 10.
program.eduIdea: Understanding chronic pain to regain confidence: it’s real, but it doesn’t mean the back is damaged. Then lifestyle, pain management and acceptance and commitment.
program.eduProgress: One 5-minute lesson per active day, in order, with a question at each step.
program.medIdea: Living with pain rather than fighting it. Secular mindfulness, practised in sessions, then useful during the day.
program.medProgress: One guided session per practice, then free sessions with short reminders. 10 minutes in week 1, 15 after, up to 30 if wanted.
medThemes: The breath, and coming back when the mind wanders
The body scan, from head to feet
Kindness: talking to yourself as to a friend
What matters: stopping the struggle, thoughts as clouds, your values
program.walkIdea: Getting back into walking. A goal in minutes per week, never per day: a bad day can be made up later, or not at all.
program.walkProgress: It starts from what the person already walks (at least 15 minutes a week) and aims for about double in 8 weeks, from 45 to 125 minutes: about 10% more each week. Pain above 3/10: same goal. Two weeks in a row: walk as much as possible under 3/10, and start again from there.
program.walkExample: Starting at 30 minutes a week: 30, 33, 37, 40, 45, 49, 54, then 60 minutes.
